newsitem.title: USA: Jordan's queen expresses doubts about peace process.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's queen expresses doubts about peace process.

text.p: Jordan's Queen Noor said on Tuesday the Middle East peace process between Israel and its neighbours could collapse entirely after recent setbacks.
"The danger of the peace process collapsing is entirely real," the queen told students at Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government.
This danger is a reversal of recent trends, which appeared to have ushered in a new era of better relations between Israel and neighbouring states, Queen Noor said.
"Until recently, we, in Jordan, had been firmly convinced that the historic peace process in the Middle East was irreversible," she said.

"However, the lack of implementations of accords reached on the Palestinian-Israeli track and, to some extent on some of the bilateral agreements between Jordan and Israel, and the alarming deterioration of the situation in the Middle East have clearly highlighted the fragility of the progress so far achieved and shaken our belief that the peace process is irreversible," she said in her prepared remarks.
She called on the United States and the international community, "especially Europe, which has historic responsibilities in the region," to help with the peace process.

The queen, in response to a student's question, said last week's Washington summit between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "did in fact succeed in bringing together the parties involved in face-to-face talks ... very frank, open discussions."
